evals.prompt: Can you review this function? Does it look right, or is there anything you'd clean up?
evals.expected_output: A function with two restating comments, an any-typed param with a hiding 'as unknown as' cast, and two boolean call-site parameters. Flags all four using the skill's specific WHAT-vs-WHY comment framing and casting/hiding-vs-resolving framing, not just generic praise.
expectations: Flags the leading comment as restating what the function already says, not explaining why
Flags the second comment ('increment the counter by 1') the same way -- pure restatement
Flags the two boolean parameters as a call-site readability problem
Flags the 'as unknown as' cast as hiding a real type mismatch, not resolving one
Does not just say the code looks fine or give only generic/vague praise

evals.prompt: is this idiomatic? getTotal creates a PriceCalculator instance just to call one method on it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the class has no state/identity/polymorphism need and recommends a plain function instead. Non-discriminating in practice (a capable baseline reasons through this correctly too) -- useful as a sanity check, not a differentiator.
expectations: Identifies that the class has no state, identity, or polymorphism need -- a class isn't justified
Recommends a plain function instead of a class with one method
Does not just approve the code as-is

evals.expected_output: Identifies a needless sequential-await pattern (should be Promise.all) and an in-place mutation of a caller-owned array argument. Non-discriminating in practice.
expectations: Identifies the two independent awaits should run concurrently via Promise.all
Flags the array-argument mutation via .push as mutating caller-owned state
Does not just reformat the code without addressing either substantive issue

evals.prompt: review these two functions for naming
evals.expected_output: A function whose name hides a side effect, plus a boolean named like a noun and two type-only placeholder names. Non-discriminating in practice.
expectations: Flags a function name that hides a side effect its name gives no hint of
Flags a boolean-typed variable named like a noun instead of a yes/no question
Flags placeholder single-letter/type-only names as carrying no meaning beyond their type
Does not just approve the names as fine

evals.prompt: does this barrel file look right?
evals.expected_output: A barrel file using 'export *' across two source files. DISCRIMINATING: a baseline run reached the wrong top-line verdict ('basically correct as-is, no changes required') and buried the issue as a non-blocking note; the skill correctly led with 'not quite right' and named export * as the actual problem.
expectations: Flags 'export *' as silently expanding the module's public API as the primary finding, not a footnote
Recommends explicit named re-exports instead
Does not conclude the barrel file is correct as-is / requires no changes
